title: Route decision & fallback scenarios for SLO preservation
content:
Purpose:
This note records a compact operational runbook embedded in architecture decisions for routing and control-plane behavior during partial-region degradation and capacity-constrained incidents. Audience: on-call platform engineers, incident commander (IC), and on-call SREs responsible for inference routing and control-plane decisions.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to user-facing routing decisions for inference requests (hosted and dedicated) across multi-region clusters (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1, apac1).
- Assumes control plane can: read regional health and capacity metrics, apply routing policy overrides, and trigger traffic-weight updates or blacklists for model variants.
- Not a exhaustive network-runbook; assumes lower-level networking (peering, transit) runbooks exist.

High-level architecture summary (1-paragraph):
The control plane maintains a region-state map built from health probes, telemetry (p999 latency, 95th tail queue depth), and capacity signals (available GPU slots, batching headroom). A routing policy engine computes per-route decisions: prefer lowest-cost region that meets SLO thresholds; failover prefers region affinity by customer/tenant when possible. Circuit-breakers are configured per model and per region with escalating thresholds that automatically reduce traffic to a region and cascade to fallback models.

Key routing policies (concise):
- SLO-first: Any region with rolling p99 > 800ms or queue_depth > 200 triggers immediate weight reduction.
- Soft degradation: Reduce weight in 10% increments every 30s up to 60% before hard cutover.
- Hard cutover: If p99 > 2s or error rate > 5% for 2 minutes, region is quarantined for 15m.
- Cost-aware fallback: If top-regions are degraded, prefer next region with SLO adherence even if cost delta <20%.
- Tenant affinity: Enterprise tenants with dedicated capacity keep affinity unless region capacity is <20% of SLA commit.

Operational signals and dashboards to check (quick list):
- Grafana: controlplane/routing/region-state-overview (p50/p95/p99, qdepth, slot-availability)
- Prometheus: controlplane_request_latency_seconds_bucket{region=~".*"}
- Logs: controlplane-routing-decisions (search trace_id from request)
- Alerts: PLAT-ROUTE-DEGRADE (p99 latency), PLAT-CAPACITY-SHORTAGE, PLAT-REGION-ERRORBURST
- Traces: jaeger.service=controlplane, span=route_evaluate

Triage checklist (first 8 minutes):
1) Identify scope: which region(s) and which models/routes are impacted? (Use dashboard filters, sample request ids.)
2) Confirm source: control-plane decision vs infra (node failures) vs network (peering). Look at node health and k8s events.
3) If control-plane made bulk weight adjustments in the past 5 minutes, inspect config commits (GH PRs) and active overrides.
4) If node-level: check node autoscaler, GPU health, and recent deploys.
5) Determine SLO risk: estimate % of traffic above latency SLO and which tenants exceed thresholds.
6) Notify IC and move to containment steps.

Containment & mitigation (ordered steps):
- Automated path (preferred when runbook triggers exist):
  * If PLAT-ROUTE-DEGRADE fires for a region and p99 > 1s for 1m: control plane will trigger soft-degrade (10% weight decrement) automatically. Monitor for 2 cycles.
  * If degradation persists and meets hard cutover criteria: automated quarantine (set region weight=0 for affected routes) with an alert to on-call.
- Manual emergency actions (if automation not functioning or manual override needed):
  1) Execute emergency partial-deprioritization to preserve SLOs:
     - Command: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/override -d '{"route":"<route>","region":"us-west1","action":"deprioritize","amount":0.6,"ttl":900}'
     - Sanity check: GET /api/v1/override/<id> then confirm via routing dashboard.
  2) If system is saturated (queue_depth > 400): enable regional circuit-breaker for model="<model>" with threshold 200 qdepth.
     - Command: cpctl circuits set --region us-west1 --model <model> --queue-threshold 200 --duration 900s
  3) Redirect non-critical traffic (batch jobs, low-priority tenants) to maintenance pool:
     - Tagging: /api/v1/tenants/<id>/set-priority?priority=low
     - Confirm via tenants table and cost dashboard.

Escalation and coordination (who to page and when):
- Pager: Platform on-call (primary). If region quarantine > 15m or >5% customers affected -> Page Eng Leads (Asha Patel) and SRE Manager (Marcos Rivera).
- Slack channels: #plat-oncall, #infra-ops, #prod-incidents. Use /incident create with incident tag PLAT-REGION-FALLBACK.
- External comms: If >2 enterprise tenants degrade, notify account execs via CS playbook (CS lead Evelyn Park).

Rollback & recovery checklist (post-mitigation):
1) Observe 10 minutes of stable p99 and qdepth for the fallback region and origin.
2) Start a staged ramp-back: reintroduce weight in 20% increments every 60s (monitoring for regressions).
3) If latency or error resurges, revert ramp and extend quarantine by TTL.
4) Record exact overrides and lifecycle to linked_artifacts (GH PR or controlplane audit id).

Concrete incident scenarios (3 succinct examples):
Scenario A — Gradual capacity erosion in us-west1 due to batch job leak:
- Symptoms: p95 rising, qdepth slowly climbs over 20 minutes, node autoscaler not reclaiming.
- Action: immediately soft-deprioritize user-facing routes. Investigate batch job via k8s jobs namespace. Patch job or move it to maintenance pool. Ramp-back after cluster stabilizes 30m.

Scenario B — Sudden region-wide network flap (peering) causing intermittent timeouts:
- Symptoms: 5xx spike, request timeouts, control-plane health probes for region show 503.
- Action: perform hard quarantine (set region weight=0) for affected routes, escalate to network team, enable alternative regions. Communicate to customers if impact >10 minutes.

Scenario C — Control-plane misconfiguration deploy changed matching rules, causing misrouting to low-capacity variant:
- Symptoms: sudden shift in routing decision logs correlated with recent PR merge.
- Action: rollback control-plane deploy (kubectl rollout undo deployment/controlplane) OR revert config via cpctl config revert --commit <sha>. Validate by replaying small test traffic.

Safety and operational limits (do not exceed):
- Never increase regional weight beyond 100% of configured route capacity without explicit approval from Eng Leads.
- Do not disable tenant affinity for enterprise customers unless authorized by SRE Manager and CS.

Post-incident: minimal required artefacts within 48 hours:
- Incident timeline (timestamps, commands executed, owners) as a one-pager attached to JIRA-PLAT-847.
- Root cause hypothesis and next steps (short list of engineering tasks).
- Test plan to exercise the failing path in staging and a rollback test.

Runbook quick commands cheat-sheet (examples):
- Check region p99: curl -s 'https://grafana.internal/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/ds/query' -d '{"query":"histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(controlplane_request_latency_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le,region))"}'
- View active overrides: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/overrides
- Apply emergency override: cpctl override apply --route <route> --region us-west1 --deprioritize 0.6 --ttl 900
- Revert override: cpctl override delete --id <override-id>

Open questions / follow-ups tracked here:
- Add capability to run canary-weighted failover automatically per-tenant. (owner: Asha)
- Improve observability for queue depth per-tenant to enable safer soft-degrades. (owner: Marcos)
- Add synthetic-slo probes for models that exercise KV-cache behavior across regions. (owner: Evelyn)

Notes and context links:
- Decision rationale: prefer SLO-preserving traffic routing over cost-savings when degradation is detected.
- Related architecture doc: confluence page linked in linked_artifacts.
- This runbook is intentionally compact — detailed runbooks for node/network and tenant-CS playbooks exist elsewhere.
